titulo: A law firm's website, before and after
hooks: Does your firm's site say Not Secure?
A lawyer with a generic email raises doubts
Lawyers: what your clients see first
voz: A law firm runs on trust. If the browser shows a Not Secure warning and you reply from a generic free email, that trust is gone before the first consultation. With your own domain, the padlock and clear copy, the client walks into the meeting already convinced.
captions: At a law firm, clients judge how serious you are before the first meeting. A Not Secure warning or a generic email makes them hesitate right there.
An email like contact@yourfirm.com says more than any diploma on the wall. And you get it with your website's domain.
Endless paragraphs in gray text don't explain anything to anyone. Your client wants to know in two lines whether you can help with their case.
fuente: Chromium Blog (2018): starting with Chrome 68, all HTTP pages are marked "Not secure".
